Name: Demetrius, the Silversmith
Summary: Demetrius was a silversmith at Ephesus who made silver shrines of Diana and stirred up his fellow craftsmen against Paul, fearing their trade and the goddess's honour would fall. The uproar filled the theatre for two hours with cries of Great is Diana. He is distinct from Demetrius of the later epistles.
KeyStory: Demetrius counted his profits in shrines and cried that Paul had turned the city from Diana.
LifeLesson: When the gospel threatens a trade, the trade fights back. Demetrius named his god's honour and meant his income.
